rounds.text: Coral Laboratories is fundamentally mispriced relative to its intrinsic value, trading at a modest P/E of 10.8x against a sector benchmark of 30.78x [E1, E6]. This deep discount extends to its Price-to-Book ratio of 1.05x compared to the sector's 3.01x, and an EV/EBITDA of 4.94x versus the sector's 16.42x [E7, E11]. Backing this valuation, a discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of Rs 843 per share against the current market price of Rs 664, providing a meaningful margin of safety of 21.3% [E43, E44]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF indicates that the current market price implies an unrealistic -0.4% earnings growth, failing to credit the company's recent acceleration [E45]. Operational momentum is strong, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 28% and profit growth of 24%, alongside stellar recent screen metrics including 91% YoY sales growth and 46% YoY net profit growth [E17, E21, E56, E58]. The balance sheet remains exceptionally robust with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.06x and a pristine cash conversion rate of 1.00x where profits are fully backed by operating cash flows of Rs 16 Cr [E34, E35, E37]. Conceded: [E14] compounded sales growth over 10 years sits at a stagnant 1%.

Coral Laboratories Ltd carries fundamental operational weakness masked by low headline valuation multiples, underscored by a dismal 10-year compounded sales growth of 1% [E14] and a 5-year compounded sales growth of -2.31% [E52]. The business suffers from persistently low profitability, evidenced by a 3-year low return on equity of 10.1% [E53], a recent ROE of 7.8% [E13], and a median 5-year ROE of just 8% [E27]. Furthermore, reported earnings quality is compromised by the inclusion of Rs. 9.52 Cr in other income [E54], while the company's financial position shows strain through negative free cash flow of Rs -5 Cr in Mar 2026 [E36] alongside borrowings surging to Rs 13 Cr from Rs 4 Cr a year prior [E38]. Expectations have also run ahead of actual underlying delivery, as demonstrated by 5-year share price growth of 16% outpacing a 3% profit growth over the same period [E19, E23, E46]. Conceded: the company trades at a modest P/E of 10.8x and P/B of 1.05x against sector benchmarks [E1, E2, E6, E7], and delivered a strong 28% TTM sales growth [E17] alongside 1.00x cash conversion of profits [E34].

Conceded: long-term growth metrics are subdued, with 10-year compounded sales growth at 1% [E14] and 5-year sales growth at -2.31% [E52], alongside a modest 5-year median ROE of 8% [E27]. However, the bear overlooks a major operational inflection: trailing twelve-month sales growth has surged to 28% [E17], complemented by a 3-year compounded profit growth of 36% [E20] and a 24% increase in TTM profit growth [E21]. The concern regarding cash generation and borrowings is mitigated by the fact that operating cash flow reached Rs 16 Cr with a pristine 1.00x cash conversion matching reported profit [E34, E35], while the debt-to-equity ratio remains highly conservative at 0.06x [E37]. Conceded: earnings contain other income of Rs 9.52 Cr [E54], but this coexists with a solid operating margin of 20% that expanded by 1 percentage point over three years [E30]. Finally, valuation fears are entirely decoupled from current pricing reality, as a reverse DCF demonstrates that the market price of Rs 664 already prices in a negative earnings growth of -0.4%, leaving a healthy 21.3% margin of safety against the base case intrinsic value [E2, E43, E45].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month sales growth has surged to 28% [E17] and 3-year compounded profit growth is 36% [E20]. However, the bull's focus on recent acceleration ignores the company's entrenched secular stagnation, characterized by a 10-year compounded sales growth of just 1% [E14] and a 5-year contraction of -2% [E15]. This historical top-line failure is mirrored in the return profile, where the bull's cited median ROE figures disguise chronically low returns of 8% over the past year and a 5-year median of just 8% [E27, E29]. Furthermore, the pristine cash conversion [E34] and low debt ratio [E37] do not negate the alarming plunge into negative free cash flow, which stood at Rs -5 Cr in March 2026 [E36], alongside a sudden surge in borrowings to Rs 13 Cr from Rs 4 Cr a year prior [E38]. The bull downplays earnings quality, yet reported profits are heavily flattered by a massive other income component of Rs 9.52 Cr [E54]. Finally, the claim that valuation is decoupled from reality [E45] overlooks the scanX signal engine warnings that price growth is outstripping fundamentals, explicitly noting that 5-year price growth of 16% has vastly outpaced a profit growth of 3% [E46].
